findings.finding: The supplied structure is the original common receptor/bound-ligand input, not a generated Steer structure; it contains 308 protein heavy atoms in the crop and has no affinity labels.

The receptor crop is centered at [23.35, -30.94, 13.33] Å with a 12 Å radius and contains 308 protein heavy atoms; nearest-protein-neighbor distance quantiles are approximately 1.23, 1.37, and 3.90 Å.

directions: Treat the pocket field as an untyped geometric proxy rather than a physical affinity energy; use modest contact weights (0 or 0.1/0.25) as candidate settings and assess outcomes with the specified final FLOWR predicted target pIC50 objective.

Because the supplied neighbor-distance quantiles include very short distances, compare repulsion weights 1 and 2 as a geometry-checking sensitivity experiment; these coordinates alone do not establish that stronger repulsion improves affinity.
Compare native_rms_ratio 0.2 and 0.33 and time_ramp_power 0 and 1 as permitted pocket-field sensitivities, while allowing graph transitions as specified.
limitations: The evidence contains only receptor geometry, no affinity labels, generated designs, measured outcomes, or observed comparisons; it cannot support enrichment, selection-survival, temporal-trend, or causal-effect estimates.
The nearest-neighbor quantiles do not specify atom-pair identities or a full contact/clash analysis, so they cannot identify particular residues or ligand interaction motifs.
The pocket objective omits ligand attraction and is explicitly an untyped geometric proxy; proposed parameter settings are new design hypotheses, not statistically supported findings.
